summary:
All seven fixes owed from the last round (O-024 to O-030) are in the tree and hold, and I found nothing new worth a finding.

**What I ran:**
- Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Core tests: 296 passed. Fitness: all 47 rules hold.
- I checked that the published exe (built 01:21:42) is newer than the last source edit (01:20:51), then probed it in a live scan with a throwaway startup hook in %TEMP%.
  - When the menu opens on a results-list row, the app captures that row (a1) into the menu's Tag and points the item's command at the Window.
  - After a live refresh the row's container is detached and holds WPF's disconnected placeholder item ({DisconnectedItem}). The menu stays open with Tag still a1, and the item stays enabled; CanExecute against its own target is True.
  - That is the case round three measured as disabled, and it now works.

**What I checked by reading:**
- The window-level ContextMenuOpening handler and the old type-name guard are gone.
- The disconnected placeholder is now detected with ReferenceEquals, and a missing row is stored as a NoRow stand-in that disables the entry.
- The Failed and "no longer exists" status texts now lead with the outcome and put the path last.
- The reveal hook no longer writes the menu's Tag, and R-001 now requires the app itself to have captured the row.
- The placeholder step draws a real placeholder container, opens its own menu, and must report found, captured and disabled.
- Explorer windows the case opened are closed before every step, 'dup.' runs before the root step, and the decoy check polls for 2 s.
- The 'top' step waits for its row to appear before stopping the scan.
- B-007 and B-008 now prove the status line was on screen and one line tall, and B-007 gained the Completed-ending variant.
- The layout comment in MainWindow.xaml now matches what I measured earlier: 398.3 px with the status line, 420.2 px without.

I did not run R-001 myself, because it opens Explorer windows and calls Quit() on the ones it opened. Its passes are the builder's.

**Checked and deliberately not filed:**
- **Line breaks in Windows error messages.** 423 of about 4,500 Win32 messages contain line breaks, and a one-line, trimmed status text still breaks at them (measured 31.92 px for two lines). The window's minimum height leaves 44 px spare for the status line, so a clip needs a message of three or more lines at the minimum window size. The failures a reveal realistically hits (0x80070005, 0x80070035, 0x80070043, 0x800704CF, 0x8007052E) are all one line, so I recorded this as drift instead.
- **The builder's reason for NoRow is wrong, but the code is fine.** The builder says each list's rows share one context menu. I measured separate menu instances on TopLevelList rows 0 and 1, because `x:Shared="False"` gives one per container. NoRow is still harmless, and the stale-row case it guards against only exists for a container that is recycled while scrolling.

My temporary folders are removed and the worktree is unchanged.

Second round: I found nothing new this round; every new parser, matcher and boundary in the latest fix-round diff held up.

**Parsers and matchers**
- **CheckStatusShown.** Its `Field` lookup (WindowCases.ps1:471-472) needs the start of the line or a space before `key=`. So 'status' cannot match inside 'statusHeight=', and a missing or duplicated 'drives in' line gives '' and fails the check. The hook writes 'True' and the height with InvariantCulture, and the test parses them the same way.
- **RevealMode's surface split regex.** Adding 'top-live' is safe. The regex backtracks from 'top' to 'top-live' when the ':' does not follow, and `hasTopTarget` tests the prefix 'top:', which 'top-live:' does not start with.
- **Name matching.** WaitForTopRow matches the target name exactly or by suffix. Among New-TopsTree's names only 'a1-<planted>' ends with the target. The 'tree:root' target matches the root row by suffix ('…\reveal-root').

**Boundaries in the app**
- **Before the menu first opens.** The MenuItem has no CommandTarget, so WPF routes from the MenuItem itself and the entry is disabled while the menu is closed. Opened then sets the target to the Window before it sets Tag. The Tag change re-queries CanExecute against the new target. I measured the entry enabled at open and still enabled after a live refresh.
- **Missing or detached row.** A null PlacementTarget or the disconnected sentinel becomes NoRow. PathOf maps NoRow to "", so it neither acts nor falls through to the keyboard-focused row.
- **Ctrl+Enter.** It still resolves the focused row, and it cannot fire from inside the open menu's popup.

**Test paths**
- Every 'via=menu' line must carry `captured=true`, so a click-failed line with a null value fails.
- The placeholder hold-back keeps the TreeView's own Expanded handler from running only for that one expansion.
- Windows are closed with a 5 s cap, and only those absent from the baseline.

The one boundary that does give way is an error message containing line breaks, which makes the status line taller than one line. It was measured and recorded as drift in the first round, and is not re-filed.

obligations.evidence: Closed by the O-024 work. MainWindow.xaml.cs OnRowContextMenuOpened captures the row into Tag and sets each MenuItem's CommandTarget to the Window. Measured in the published exe mid-scan: after a refresh, containerDc={DisconnectedItem} and inTree=False, while menuOpen=True, tag=TopLevelRow:a1, enabled=True and CanExecute(param, target)=True.
WindowCases.ps1 Test-R001 feeds every missing shape. With the O-025 changes, the 'dup.' ancestor check can now fail: windows are closed before each step and 'dup.' runs before the root step.

MainWindow.xaml: the MenuItem's CommandTarget binding to PlacementTarget is removed. MainWindow.xaml.cs:~716-725: OnRowContextMenuOpened sets item.CommandTarget = this (line 722) and Tag to the row. Measured: the entry stays enabled after a live refresh detaches the container. R-001's top-live step asserts detached, scanning, open, enabled, the revealed path and the Explorer selection.

WindowCases.ps1 Test-R001: $closeNewWindows quits the non-baseline hwnds, waits and asserts none are left before every step. 'dup.' (step 3) runs before tree:root (step 4). The decoy check polls the $root windows for 2 s.

RevealMode.cs OpenMenu sets only PlacementTarget and IsOpen and never writes Tag; 'captured' is read from the app's Tag. Invoke-RevealRun requires captured=true on every via=menu line. ProcessPlaceholder realizes a real placeholder container by holding back Expanded once, opens that container's own menu, and logs found/captured/disabled, all three of which R-001 step 13 requires.

StartupHook.cs HoldForDrives appends ' status=<b> statusHeight=<px>' when FSA_HOOK_STATUS is set. WindowCases.ps1 CheckStatusShown asserts visible and height+6 <= 24. It is called from Invoke-StoppedEnding when $statusMsg is given and from B-007's new Completed variant, which also runs CheckBothLists with the folder tree.
RevealMode.cs Drive: for a 'top:' target it calls WaitForScanToStart, then WaitForTopRow(window, targetName), then StopScan. top-live also waits for its row before opening the menu.

MainWindow.xaml.cs FormatRevealStatus: Failed is "Couldn't open Explorer: <msg> (0x<hr>). '<requested>'" and NoLongerExists is "No longer exists, so highlighting '<shown>' instead: '<requested>'". The catch block in OnOpenInExplorer uses the same Failed order.

MainWindow.xaml.cs OnRowContextMenuOpened: `menu.Tag = row is null || ReferenceEquals(row, BindingOperations.DisconnectedSource) ? NoRow : row`. NoRow maps to "" in PathOf, so the entry is disabled. The window-level ContextMenuOpening handler and both GetType().Name comparisons are removed (MainWindow.xaml:6 no longer names the handler).

cases.evidence: R-001's top-live step feeds a results-list row during a running scan. It waits until a live refresh detaches the row's container, then asserts the entry is enabled and that the click reveals that row (Exact, with Explorer selection). The unreadable-row step and the stopped-scan top step remain.
tree-competing selects the root row, then opens nested inner.bin's own menu. The row now comes only from the app's Opened handler (captured=true is required), not from the hook.
The placeholder step draws a real NotOpenedYet container and opens its own RowContextMenu. R-001 requires found, captured and disabled.
The 'dup.' step now runs in a clean window state, asserts the ancestor is selected in a window that step opened, and polls for 2 s that the decoy is never selected.

drift: The build's declared reason for storing NoRow says the RowContextMenu 'is one instance shared by that list's rows'. In the published exe, TopLevelList rows 0 and 1 have different ContextMenu instances, because x:Shared="False" gives one per container. NoRow is still a safe choice, but the stale Tag it guards against can only come from a container recycled by scrolling that keeps its own menu, not from a menu shared across rows.

The XAML comment (MainWindow.xaml:155-158) and CheckStatusShown both treat RevealStatus as one line. A NoWrap TextBlock still breaks at explicit line breaks, and 423 of about 4,500 FACILITY_WIN32 messages contain them (274 with two lines, the rest with 3 to 41). A Failed status carrying one measured 31.92 px for two lines. At 644 px there are 44 px spare, so only a message of 3 or more lines clips the lists at the minimum size. The common reveal errors are all one line. If it ever matters, `.ReplaceLineEndings(" ")` on the Win32 message in FormatRevealStatus and in the catch block closes it.

The design's contract text ('CommandParameter = PlacementTarget.DataContext'; the context menu's command targets the row) no longer describes the code. The row is captured into the menu's Tag when it opens, and the command is sent to the Window. The CommandTarget choice is declared and the Tag capture was the accepted m1 fix, but no design document records the resulting mechanism.
